The reds are ledger-recorded fail/pass pairs, not claims.

C-TEACHING-INCREMENT-1-B9D139EA.Problem: Seven staged findings, each measured and each naming this increment as its owner, are open at once. `F296` (`ngrace-execute` rule 5 ends "batch the fix, not the guards", which assumes guards can be driven red one at a time) has no rule for an indivisible mechanism whose guards can only green together, so the only red-first path is the retrospective red `F283` forbids; `F298` measured the one fact `F296` was gated on — the attempt-pair audit pairs attempts, not test cases, so one `fail`/`pass` pair covers an N-guard cluster. `F283` measured a cursor `fail` recorded *after* the fix that greens it, uncorroborated because `WriteEvidence` digests at attempt time. `F285` measured a plan whose `ObservedWriteScope` omitted the record files the authority's close wrote, and the close's `ngrace review` returned three `review.scope-outside-write-scope` errors — the cost was a bundle supersede. `F293` measured a spec whose own byte-invariance criterion forbade the write its `Pays` line required, with the payer-map repair outside its declared scope: the fifth instance of one class and the second after its own finding was written. `F290` measured structural claims about XML artifacts answered by regex and by an XPath that assumed the wrong nesting — four misses, three tools, one cause: writing a pattern from an assumed shape. `F302` measured that `TaughtIn` has a reader (`scripts/record-query.ts`), a validator (`taughtResolvesCheck`) and a schema slot (`record-serialize.ts`) but no writer, so under the CLI-only-writes direction the annotation `D41` anticipates cannot be produced by any permitted act.
